links.outcome: Hallucination rate in AI chest X-ray readings rated by two radiologists
links.effect: KARA-CXR non-hallucination rate 75% vs ChatGPT 38%; hallucinations frequent, especially in ChatGPT. Interobserver agreement 0.91 (KARA) and 0.85 (GPT4).
links.quote: KARA-CXR demonstrated a non-hallucination rate of 75%, which is significantly higher than ChatGPT's 38%.

links.outcome: Comparison of candidate AI systems on same chest X-ray data for accuracy
links.effect: KARA-CXR rated 'Acceptable' 70.50% and 68.00% by two observers vs ChatGPT 40.50% and 47.00%; KARA-CXR significantly more accurate.
links.quote: In the 'Acceptable' accuracy category, KARA-CXR was rated at 70.50% and 68.00% by two observers, while ChatGPT achieved 40.50% and 47.00%.

screen.reason: The study retrospectively evaluates and compares the performance and safety/hallucination profiles of two multimodal/LLM-based chest X-ray interpretation models (KARA-CXR vs ChatGPT) using radiologist grading, but does not test a specific organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
